title: River Review QA Evidence
description: Untrusted user input recording the result of QA the consumer ran themselves (ADR-017 D3 / D5). The SSoT for every field, requirement and failure treatment is `docs/development/qa-evidence-contract.md`; this schema is its stage-1 / stage-3 structural check (§7). Encoding rule: every object is closed (`additionalProperties: false`), every value is typed, every string has `maxLength` and every array has `maxItems`, so an undefined field or a wrong type rejects the whole document as `QA_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED` and an over-long string or over-long array rejects it as `QA_EVIDENCE_TOO_LARGE`. The deterministic module validates with Ajv 2020 (`ajv/dist/2020.js`) plus `ajv-formats` under `strict: true`; `ajv-formats` is required because `attempts[].startedAt` uses `format: date-time`, which strict Ajv refuses to compile without it. `required`, `pattern`, `enum` and `const` are used ONLY where the contract rejects the whole document; a field whose absence or invalid value the contract treats as `do not count` (for example `basis`, `expected.source`, `execution.runner`, `environment.os`, `attempts[].command`, `refs[].sha256`) is typed and length-bounded here but not required or enumerated, because the deterministic module must count it as unverified instead of rejecting. Limits that JSON Schema cannot express are enforced by the deterministic module before schema validation: the evidence document is at most 1,048,576 bytes of UTF-8 and at most 16 levels of nesting; each referenced artifact is at most 104,857,600 bytes and all referenced artifacts together at most 536,870,912 bytes (`QA_ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE`). Semantics outside this schema are decided by the deterministic module, never by this schema: id normalization with `nonEmptyNfcString` and uniqueness (§4.2), the C / T / V set comparison (§4.3), the verified conditions (§5), sha256 comparison and the artifact read rules (§3.5), the HEAD and `dirty` comparison (§5 condition 5), attempt ordering, status-to-last-attempt agreement and `passed <= total` (§3.4). Passing this schema never makes an acceptance criterion verified.

verification.description: One result per confirmed AC (§3.4). Duplicate or unknown `acId` and the C / T / V comparison are decided by the deterministic module (§4.3).

id.description: AC id or artifact id (§4.2). This schema checks only the type and the raw length (160, leaving room for surrounding whitespace). The character set and the 128-character limit apply to the NORMALIZED value: the deterministic module normalizes with `nonEmptyNfcString` (trim, then NFC) and then requires 1 to 128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` (`QA_TARGET_AC_ID_INVALID` / `QA_ARTIFACT_ID_INVALID`). A raw pattern cannot express that order, because NFC can turn a non-ASCII value into an ASCII one (U+212A KELVIN SIGN becomes `K`).

repository.description: GitHub `owner/name` only in the first version (owner up to 39 characters, name up to 100). Invalid rejects the whole document (`QA_TARGET_REPOSITORY_INVALID`).

subjectRevision.description: Full 40- or 64-digit hex commit id; short SHAs are rejected (`QA_TARGET_REVISION_INVALID`). Lower-cased by the deterministic module, which also compares it with the HEAD River Review observed (§5 condition 5).

acceptanceCriteria.description: The AC list as the evidence states it (T). It is compared with the confirmed list, never trusted as the population (§4.1, §4.3).

required.description: Accepted but never read: required / optional comes from the confirmed AC list (§3.1, §4.1).

expected.description: Fixed expected result. A missing `value` or `source` counts the AC as unverified, not a whole-document rejection, so neither is required here.

value.description: Missing: `QA_TARGET_EXPECTED_MISSING`. Compared with the confirmed list before redaction (§5 condition 7).

source.description: `sourced` / `reproduced` / `derived` (§5). Missing or any other value counts the AC as unverified (`QA_TARGET_EXPECTED_SOURCE_MISSING`), decided by the deterministic module.

sourceRef.description: Artifact id the expected value comes from; required by the deterministic module when `source` is `sourced` (`QA_TARGET_EXPECTED_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED`).

execution.description: §3.2. A missing `runner` counts every AC as unverified (`QA_EXECUTION_RUNNER_MISSING`).

ciRun.description: Reference to a CI run. Recorded only; never a basis for independence (§6).

environment.description: §3.3. A missing `os` counts every AC as unverified (`QA_ENVIRONMENT_INCOMPLETE`).

status.description: Invalid rejects the whole document (`QA_VERIFICATION_STATUS_INVALID`). Agreement with the last attempt is checked by the deterministic module (`QA_VERIFICATION_STATUS_MISMATCH`).

basis.description: `verified` / `explore`. Missing or any other value counts the AC as unverified (`QA_VERIFICATION_BASIS_MISSING`), decided by the deterministic module.

attempts.description: Every attempt, strictly ascending by `startedAt` (checked by the deterministic module: `QA_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPTS_UNORDERED`). Empty for `PASS` / `FAIL` counts the AC as unverified (`QA_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPTS_EMPTY`), so there is no `minItems` here.

notRunReason.description: `criteria-ambiguous` / `environment-unavailable` / `out-of-scope` / `execution-failed` / `requires-human-judgment`, expected for `SKIP` / `NOT_RUN`. This is the only vocabulary for why a result is `SKIP` / `NOT_RUN`; a consumer maps any external tool's reason codes onto it before handing the evidence over. Missing or any other value is recorded as `QA_VERIFICATION_REASON_MISSING` by the deterministic module; it does not reject the document.

subcases.description: Cases inside one AC (§3.4.1), for example the normal path and a permission error. A non-empty `subcases` forbids the AC's own `basis`, `attempts` and `notRunReason`. The deterministic module checks that subcase ids are unique within the AC (`QA_VERIFICATION_SUBCASE_ID_INVALID`) and that the AC `status` equals the worst subcase status, ordered FAIL > NOT_RUN > SKIP > PASS (`QA_VERIFICATION_SUBCASE_STATUS_MISMATCH`). An empty array means no subcases.

controls.description: Control runs on a revision before the change, expected to FAIL (§3.4.2). Recorded only in the first version: they are not a verified condition. A missing control (`QA_CONTROL_MISSING`) or a control that passed (`QA_CONTROL_PASSED`) is kept in the audit result's Gaps by the deterministic module.

subcase.description: Same rules as an AC result (§3.4.1). The id follows §4.2 and is unique within the AC.

control.description: One run of the same check on a revision before the change (§3.4.2). River Review does not confirm that `revision` precedes the change; it is self-reported (§10).

revision.description: Full 40- or 64-digit hex commit id the control ran on. Invalid rejects the whole document (`QA_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED`).

startedAt.description: RFC 3339 date-time with a mandatory time-zone offset (`Z` or `+09:00`); fractional seconds are allowed. Missing or unparseable rejects the whole document (`QA_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPT_INVALID`); ordering is compared on the parsed epoch milliseconds by the deterministic module.

logRef.description: Artifact id (§3.5). An id absent from `artifacts.refs` rejects the whole document (`QA_ARTIFACT_REF_UNKNOWN`), checked by the deterministic module.

assertions.description: `passed <= total` is checked by the deterministic module (`QA_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPT_INVALID`).

command.description: Command with arguments. Missing counts the AC as unverified (`QA_EXECUTION_COMMAND_MISSING`); longer than the limit rejects the whole document (`QA_EVIDENCE_TOO_LARGE`), so put a long command in an artifact and reference it. Redacted before any output or storage (§7).

exitCode.description: Integer from -2147483648 to 4294967295, or `null` when the value was not taken from a trustworthy path (for example through a pipe). The range covers POSIX exit statuses (0 to 255) and Windows exit codes, which are 32-bit values read as signed or unsigned. `null` or missing counts the AC as unverified (`QA_EXECUTION_EXIT_CODE_UNKNOWN`); a non-integer or out-of-range value rejects the whole document (`QA_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED`).

exitCodeSource.description: How `exitCode` was taken, or why it is `null`.

artifacts.description: §3.5. The evidence holds references and hashes only, never artifact bodies.

reproduction.description: Steps to re-run. Redacted before any output or storage (§7).

id.description: Unique within the evidence; uniqueness is checked by the deterministic module (`QA_ARTIFACT_ID_INVALID`).

root.description: `repository` (the target repository) or `artifacts` (the directory the host passes). Anything else rejects the whole document (`QA_ARTIFACT_PATH_REJECTED`).

path.description: Relative path from `root` with `/` separators. This schema rejects absolute paths, `..` segments, backslashes, NUL and values that start like a URL scheme or drive letter (`QA_ARTIFACT_PATH_REJECTED`). The scheme-like rule is deliberately broad: a relative name such as `trace:1.zip` is rejected too. NFC normalization, root containment, symlinks, hard links, non-regular files, `.git/` and the `shouldExcludeForContext` rules are checked by the deterministic module when reading (§3.5).

sha256.description: 64-digit hex, lower-cased and compared by the deterministic module. Missing, malformed or mismatched counts the referring ACs as unverified (`QA_ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH`), so it is length-bounded but not required or patterned here.

sensitivity.description: `restricted` (default when missing) outputs the id only, without path or size.

gaps.description: §3.6. Redacted before any output or storage.
